build.fail_witnesses: Three concretely exercised, not hypothetical: (1) THE REAL BUG. Part 6's two independently-coded invariance formulations initially DISAGREED -- the general P^-1MP block check PASSED while the B1011-style per-pair reformulation FAILED. Root cause found and fixed: `apply_mat`'s `sum(generator_of_ring_tuples, RING.zero())` silently invoked Python's tuple `+` (concatenation) instead of ring addition, because a raw `sum()` builtin was used on ring elements instead of an explicit ring.add loop. Confirmed the bug was isolated to that one helper by grepping every `sum(` call site in ring.py/roots.py/build.py -- ring.py has zero `sum()` calls (mat_mul uses explicit ring.add throughout), so every primary verdict (S symmetric, Sigma.Sigma^dagger=864I, T unitary, S unitary, L-via-two-routes match, and the primary P^-1MP block check) was already unaffected and correct; only the redundant secondary check needed the fix. After fixing, the two formulations agree exactly -- demonstrating the invariance claim is a real, checkable fact and not a tautology of the test code. (2) The independent float cross-check's phase comparison genuinely discriminates: comparing S_exact directly against the full textbook-prefactor S gives 0.816 max error (a clear miss), and only negating S_exact brings it to 2.8e-16 -- the check does not rubber-stamp an arbitrary convention, it identifies the exact, single sign difference. (3) The two independent A3 inner-product routes (Cartan-matrix/omega-basis vs GL(4)-permutation-with-sum-zero-projection) were built and cross-checked against each other on all 100 weight pairs before either was trusted for the S/T build -- had the sum-zero projection term (-sum(u)*sum(v)/4) been omitted from ip4, a common implementation slip for A_(n-1) embeddings, Sigma would not have come out symmetric or proportional-to-unitary at all, and this cross-check (run first, as a gate) would have caught it before it propagated.
